[[Category:Schrödinger equations]]
'''Schrödinger equations''', first published by [[Person:Erwin Schrödinger]] in 1927, provide a mathematical description of a quantum system.<ref>{{#cite:Q3352}}</ref>

== Time-dependent Schrödinger equation ==

{{#content:Q3376}}

== Time-independent Schrödinger equation ==

{{#content:Q3378}}

Equivalently,

$$
\hat{H}_Q\Psi=E\Psi.
$$

where $\hat H_Q$ is the [[quantum Hamiltonian]].

== Interpretation ==

The most well-accepted '''interpretation''' of the Schrödinger equations is given by [[Person:Max Born]] in 1926 (before Schrödinger officially published his famous equations:

$$
\text{Probability of finding the quantum particle at position } \vec r_1: P(\vec r = \vec r_1) \propto \rho(\vec r) = \Psi^2(\vec r).
$$

If for volume element $d\tau$, which in Cartesian space satisfies $d\tau=dx\,dy\,dz$:

$$
\int|\psi(\vec{r})|^2d\tau=1,
$$

then

$$
\text{Probability of finding the quantum particle at position } \vec r_1: P(\vec r = \vec r_1) = \rho(\vec r) = \Psi^2(\vec r).
$$

<ref>{{#cite:Q3352}}</ref>
